title: HC Kevin Stefanski reflects on Sunday Night Football matchup vs. Ravens |  Post-game Press Conference | Week 5 | Falcons vs. Ravens
headline: QB Michael Penix Jr. left the loss to Baltimore with a rib injury and imaging is pending, so his availability is the key fantasy question; CB C.J. Henderson also hurt his groin.
summary: Stefanski opened with the injury news: C.J. Henderson has a groin injury and Michael Penix Jr. has a rib injury, with imaging to come on both. He credited Baltimore as a good team and said Atlanta missed opportunities and failed to put the game away late after leading, and the game went to overtime and ended in a loss. He said Penix tried to work to get comfortable after the injury but could not return. Asked why the offense leaned less on Bijan Robinson and the run game and more on Penix than in the previous two weeks, he said it was a mix of game script and Baltimore's defensive adjustments, and the team needs to get into the end zone more. He said the run defense, which had been strong, was gashed because the team did not get off blocks or tackle well enough. He said Baltimore knocked the offense back in the run game, including in the red zone, and the team did not score enough. On Penix's play before the injury, he said Penix made some plays against a tough defense, has things to improve, and battled. Asked about supporting Penix, who was emotional on the sideline, he said he does not yet know enough and would wait for more information.

injuries.detail: Rib injury; imaging pending. He tried to get comfortable but could not return to the game.
Groin injury; more will be known after imaging.

signals.claim: Penix's availability going forward depends on imaging results on his rib injury; no timeline given.
signals.note: The starting QB's status is uncertain, which hurts Penix and the passing-game pieces, and could mean a backup QB is in the lineup.
signals.quote: He was trying to work to get comfortable and could not.

signals.claim: The offense got away from the run game versus Baltimore because of game script and the Ravens' defensive adjustments.
signals.note: Bijan's workload fell in a tough matchup and was attributed to game script, so it should rebound in a more favorable game.
signals.quote: All of the above. I think again, that's where I give credit to their defense.

signals.claim: Henderson suffered a groin injury and more will be known after imaging.
signals.note: Possible absence in the secondary could affect the defense's matchup outlook.

topics.detail: Atlanta's run defense, which had been strong, was gashed by Baltimore. Stefanski blamed poor execution on getting off blocks and tackling.
Atlanta led late but failed to finish Baltimore off and lost in overtime. Stefanski said the team will own it collectively and cited missed opportunities and thin margins.
After two games of effective red-zone running, Baltimore knocked the offense back in the run game and Atlanta did not score enough points.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Monday, October 12th | Press Conference
headline: Mike Penix Jr. (ribs) and C.J. Henderson (groin) are both being treated with no clear timeline; Stefanski will update Wednesday, so Penix's Week 7 status against Chicago is uncertain.
summary: Stefanski opened with two injuries. QB Michael Penix Jr. has a rib injury and CB C.J. Henderson has a groin injury. Both will be treated over the next couple of days, with an update on Wednesday (Penix) or later in the week (Henderson). He declined to give specifics on imaging or X-rays and would not say whether Penix could play this week. He called the loss to Baltimore frustrating, since the Falcons had chances to go up two scores in the second half and failed to close it out. He credited the Ravens for their two-minute drives, overtime drive and 200+ rushing yards, and put the blame on fundamentals, execution and the pass rush for both players and coaches. On offense, he said the deep third-down throws came from long distances created by poor first and second downs, though he praised the third-down execution and a Zachariah Branch catch-and-run for a first down. He said Penix works hard and will improve on near-miss throws such as bootlegs with a defender in his face. He praised Drake London as playing at an extremely high level and said the team will keep finding ways for him to affect the game. Cam Thomas was the game captain and was praised as playing really good football. Next up is Chicago, whom he called well coached with great players, and he said the team must prepare for every quarterback on their roster.

injuries.detail: Rib injury. Being treated, with an update coming Wednesday. Stefanski would not say whether he can play this week or discuss imaging results.
Groin injury. Being treated over the next couple of days, with an update later in the week.

signals.claim: Penix's availability for the Bears game will be clearer at Wednesday's update; no commitment that he plays.
signals.note: A rib injury with no timeline puts the QB's Week 7 status in doubt, which affects every Falcons pass-catcher.
signals.quote: I can answer that better Wednesday.

signals.claim: The Falcons will keep finding ways to get London involved in the offense.
signals.note: London is a featured piece of the offense, praised for his physicality and YAC, so he stays a high-end WR1.
signals.quote: he's playing an extremely high level

signals.note: Stefanski cited a Branch underneath catch where he broke a tackle for a first down, a small sign of trust in his role.

signals.claim: Henderson's status will be updated later this week after treatment.
signals.note: A groin injury could thin the secondary, a minor concern for IDP and defense streamers.
signals.quote: See how he responds to some treatment over the next couple of days.

topics.detail: Stefanski credited Baltimore's quarterback and plan on the late two-minute and overtime drives, and said the staff will look at how to put pass rushers in better position.
Baltimore ran for 200+ yards. Stefanski pointed to fundamentals and little things adding up, and said Wednesday's practice will focus on sound fundamentals.
The deep third-down throws came from long distances after poor first and second downs. The goal is to avoid third downs and create more manageable situations.

The Bears' quarterback situation is uncertain, so Atlanta will prepare for every QB. Stefanski noted similarities to Baltimore's run scheme through the Declan Doyle and Ben Johnson connection, but said there are plenty of differences.

title: Dave Canales: 'There’s work to do'
headline: Wharton and Moton get practice windows opened this week, Jaelan Phillips and Jalen Coker are trending toward returns, and Chuba Hubbard is the steady lead back.
summary: Canales used the bye week for self-scouting and for some injured players to get healthier. He confirmed the practice windows open this week for Tershawn Wharton and Taylor Moton. He said a fuller injury update will come later in the week, and the next step is seeing how they respond to football work. Monroe Freeling is dinged up with a knee issue but is doing everything he can to be available. Jaelan Phillips 'has a chance' to return, and Canales praised him as an every-down player who anchors the run defense. Jalen Coker had a good bye, is on track, and has a few big days ahead, starting with practice tomorrow. Chuba Hubbard got praise for his preparation and his consistency in the run game. Canales said the offense will keep using snaps under center but will decide week to week, not commit to more of it. Canales praised Nick Scott's leadership and the play of the safeties and rookie Lee Hunter. He framed the trip to Philadelphia as a high-urgency game against a hungry Eagles team and said Carter and Davis will be a challenge for the O-line.

injuries.detail: Cleared medically and his practice window opens this week. Canales said his role depends on how he responds to football work.
Cleared medically and in great shape, but he hasn't seen football yet. His window opens this week.
Dinged up with a knee issue. He is doing everything he can to be available this week.
Canales said he 'has a chance' and would give more specifics later in the week.

Canales expects the Eagles to bring urgency after a heartbreaking loss and called them a talented team. He said the O-line needs to cover up the first level against Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis. He said the Eagles' defense resembles the system the Panthers practice against.
Canales said the team will not get caught up in being alone in first place. The team's focus remains weekly improvement and preparing for a tough road environment.

title: Ben Johnson on adjustments for Week 6 | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Williams still has no return date and Chicago has not named a Week 6 starter; Tyson Bagent vs. Case Keenum is open after a five-turnover loss to Green Bay, and Kyler Gordon and Shemar Turner are still unresolved.
summary: Johnson said there were no injury updates on Monday and promised more on Wednesday. He called the loss to Green Bay poorly executed in all three phases and said the focus is fixing the run game, the pass game and explosive plays allowed on defense. He said the backfield was spread around because Kyle Monangai was active but not at full load, and the plan did not produce what he hoped. Caleb Williams is progressing and eager to return, but there is no timeline and the team is waiting for a green light. Johnson would not say whether Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum would be the first-string QB on Wednesday; he said no determination has been made. He said Bagent's turnover throws were not like what he showed in camp and that the offense could not get in rhythm (three three-and-outs, five turnovers). On defense, he took the blame, pointing to a mix of bad rushes, bad coverage and a bad call. Kyler Gordon is mentally sharp but still in a physical stress test, and Shemar Turner faces a decision on the 53-man roster within days. Chicago is 3-2 and 0-2 in the division, and heads to Atlanta next.

injuries.detail: Progressing well and itching to return, but no timeline. The team will wait for the green light before making him available.
Mentally sharp; the team is in the middle of a physical stress test to see if he is ready for games.
A decision on whether to add him to the 53-man roster is due within the next couple of days.

signals.quote: no determination has been made in terms of, uh, what direction we're going.

signals.claim: Keenum is in the mix to be the first-string QB if Williams is out.
signals.note: He could start in Atlanta, which would change the outlook for the passing game.
signals.quote: I think we have three guys that can win games in this league.

signals.claim: Bagent needs to cut down on turnovers and risky throws downfield.
signals.note: His turnovers and lack of rhythm hurt Chicago's passing offense and put his job at risk.

signals.claim: The backfield was split to spread the load because Monangai was active but not at his usual workload.
signals.note: Monangai's workload is unclear and the committee approach did not work well, so his Week 6 role is worth watching.

signals.claim: Swift ran hard on limited opportunities; Johnson wants to get the run game in rhythm.
signals.note: Johnson praised his effort but offered no commitment to more touches; script and game flow limited him.
signals.quote: He ran hard, uh, with the opportunities that he was given.

signals.note: The secondary was beaten for big plays, and his return could help it, but his status is not settled.
signals.quote: making sure that he's physically prepared to to play in football games.

signals.note: A minor IDP note: he could be activated soon.

topics.detail: Johnson said the run game and pass game both underperformed, with route running, fundamentals, technique and finish inconsistent. He is re-watching all five games to look for what has and hasn't worked, taking the QB changes into account.
Chicago must clean up explosive plays allowed. Johnson called it a collective failure involving bad rushes, bad coverage and a bad call, and took the blame himself.
The Bears are 3-2 but 0-2 in the division after losing to Green Bay. Johnson described the mood as disappointed but professional.
Johnson said Green Bay defended back-to-back perimeter plays well, and that Chicago's execution was not clean.

title: Zac Taylor Discusses Week 5, Bye Week | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bye week is a chance to heal: an unnamed player is headed to IR with a broken forearm, TE Tanner Hudson has a pec issue and S Kyle Dugger is week to week. Chase and Higgins keep getting deliberate one-on-one deep shots.
summary: Taylor opened with injuries coming out of the bye. One player (name lost in the captions) broke his forearm and will go to IR, though Taylor doesn't think it is season-ending. TE Tanner Hudson has a pec issue still being evaluated, with IR possible, and S Kyle Dugger remains week to week. He called the Week 5 win a good result but was disappointed the team didn't close it out after leading 28-10 in the fourth quarter. He called the problems easily fixable, mainly penalties and field position, and said nothing is wrong with the scheme or the personnel. He praised the run game's push up front and the backs' yards after contact, and credited TE Drew Sample's blocking and outlet work on play action. He singled out Jordan Battle for two interceptions and some strong open-field tackles. He said the offense deliberately sets up one-on-one chances for Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, who have been confident and consistent. On defense he pointed to explosive runs (crack tosses, a reverse, quarterback scrambles) as the thing to clean up, while praising the pass rush and the coverage on receivers. The bye comes at a good time with the team banged up and the Miami heat behind them. Next up is a divisional game at Baltimore.

signals.note: His availability for the Baltimore game is uncertain, which affects the safety rotation.

signals.note: He is valued for blocking and for scoring in the red zone, so he's a touchdown-dependent TE rather than a volume play.
signals.quote: He understands the proper way to do that.

signals.note: Taylor said the shot plays have paid off nearly every time they're called, which supports Higgins' upside.
signals.quote: They're really consistent.

signals.claim: The offense will keep designing one-on-one and deep shot opportunities for Chase.
signals.note: Chase keeps getting schemed shots downfield, which supports his weekly ceiling.
signals.quote: They're really consistent.

signals.note: Positive for his IDP value, and he could take on a larger role if Dugger is out.

topics.topic: Week 5 result and areas to fix
topics.detail: The team won to get its third win but didn't finish after leading 28-10 in the fourth quarter. Taylor sees penalties, field position and a few details as easy fixes and not a scheme or personnel problem.
The linemen got off the ball, the backs ran hard and got extra yards after contact, and the offense stayed ahead of the chains and had manageable third downs.

Opponents have had explosive runs on crack tosses, a reverse, traps and quarterback scrambles. Taylor wants more detail in setting the edge, though he praised the pass rush and the coverage on receivers.
Taylor praised kicker Evan for 22 consecutive made field goals, credited the snapper and holder, and said the team is comfortable asking him for long kicks.
Taylor says the bye comes at a good time. The team has played three straight close games, is banged up, and is coming off a Miami game where the heat drained them.

title: HC Sean Payton on Denver’s Week 3 takeaways: ‘We win the game yesterday because of it’
headline: Payton downplays Dobbins' big workload as game-driven, says offense has 'a ton' to fix, and keeps Bo Nix's aggressiveness 'smart' ahead of a short week vs. Seattle.
summary: Payton opened by saying the short week comes down to time and recovery, with each player's body needing to be ready for Thursday. Asked about J.K. Dobbins' season-high workload, he brushed off the idea that it was a gesture, saying the team is just trying to win games. He credited the defense's seven takeaways through five weeks, especially early punch-outs and interceptions, for winning the game, while admitting a number of things need cleanup. He praised punter Jeremy Crawshaw's consistency over the last 2-3 weeks, especially pinning a dangerous returner inside the five. On Bo Nix and the 'let it rip' comment, he said he and Nix will be on the same page each week about the plan, with some throws being aggressive and others smart. He joked about reporters carrying his comments to Nix's locker. He declined to grade Nix's confidence and said the offense is doing 'a ton' of things poorly that must improve. The next game is Thursday night against Seattle.

signals.note: Dobbins had his biggest workload yet, but Payton framed it as game-driven rather than a planned shift, so his volume is not guaranteed to continue.
signals.quote: We're trying to win games.

signals.claim: Nix will be aggressive on certain throws and smart on others, per the game plan.
signals.note: Payton didn't promise more downfield risk-taking, which tempers expectations for Nix's upside, and he said the offense has a lot to clean up.
signals.quote: there are certain throws that we're going to be aggressive with.

topics.detail: Seven takeaways through five weeks, including early punch-outs and interceptions, were key to the win. Payton said it 'can cure a lot of what ails you' but noted things to clean up.
After watching film, Payton said the offense is not doing a ton of things well and must improve before the short week.
Payton is encouraged by punter Jeremy Crawshaw's consistency over the last 2-3 weeks, including pinning a quality returner inside the five.
Preparation is limited by time and by player recovery from the last game.

title: HC Sean Payton on Week 5 vs. Chargers: ‘A hard-fought win’
headline: Broncos beat the Chargers but the offense is still sputtering (1 of ~13 on third down). Payton is simplifying the scheme, and Bo Nix needs cleaner early-game pockets.
summary: Payton called it a hard-fought win built on defense: three takeaways and a fourth-down stop on a QB sneak. He said the offense struggled badly on third down, converting only one, and that he needs to be better with protection calls against a strong front. Denver ran the ball more than it passed, and the run game improved late as the line settled in and got to the C gap. He took the blame for a delay-of-game penalty on fourth-and-goal from the one, which cost the chance to end the game on a kneel. Payton said Davis Webb's play-calling arrangement worked smoothly, with Webb offering conviction on certain plays. He is also trying to reduce the offense's variables, meaning fewer motions and shifts, so players can play faster. On Bo Nix, he said the footwork concerns are settling down, but the team needs to give him a clean pocket early in games. He also wants Nix to play more freely, and he would not blame Nix's bailing out of the pocket until he sees the tape. Looking ahead, Denver faces Seattle, the reigning champion, on a short week.

signals.claim: Denver will work to give Nix a cleaner pocket early in games and simplify the offense to help him play faster.
signals.note: Nix is still struggling through five weeks. Payton is pointing to protection, scheme and details rather than benching or blaming him, so the upside depends on fixes that haven't shown up yet.
signals.quote: I think he's settling that down.

signals.claim: Dobbins will keep getting split-zone runs as Denver leans on the ground game.
signals.note: The run game grew stronger in the second half and Dobbins looked more comfortable, which supports volume if Denver keeps running more than it passes.
signals.quote: he had some decent, you know, split side zone runs.

signals.note: Payton singled out Mims's late punt return as a big play that set up fourth-quarter field position, which mostly matters for return-yardage and special-teams scoring.
signals.quote: that was a pretty big play.

topics.detail: Payton said the arrangement with Davis Webb worked fairly smoothly on substitutions and communication. Webb brings conviction on certain plays, and the third-down plan is set during series. He said it was a difficult week emotionally and appreciated Webb's handling of it.
Denver converted only one third down, which Payton called not good enough. He cited protection calls, edge pressure and zone pressures where a guard got caught blocking a bigger linebacker.
Payton said that when output isn't there, you cut variables. The team is trimming motions and shifts so players can play faster.
The defense forced three turnovers and a fourth-down stop. Payton credited it for a good effort against a Chargers offense playing several young offensive linemen.
Payton took the blame for a delay of game on fourth-and-goal from the one after a timeout. He said he planned to kick the field goal anyway.

title: Campbell on playing complementary football
headline: Lions go into the bye on their best all-around game; Tom Kennedy is done for the year, Cade Mays is eyed for Week 7, and rookie Keith Abney got his first start at safety.
summary: Campbell called the Week 5 win at Arizona the most complete complementary game of the season, with five straight three-and-outs from the defense, a strong special teams day, and an offense that took off after the second quarter. He highlighted a fourth-and-three catch and a broken tackle by Sam LaPorta, and a fourth-and-one touchdown that started with strong protection. Rookie Keith Abney made his first NFL start at safety and was called solid, with room to grow and worth continuing to develop there. Tom Kennedy needs surgery and is out for the season, and Devin White also needs surgery and will be out a while. The team is scouting punt returners and does not want Amon-Ra St. Brown to do it full time. Cade Mays is targeted for around Week 7 after two half practices, but the staff must decide how to work a center back in and whether he can handle a full load. Campbell praised the offensive line's growth, pointing to Tate Ratledge's pad level, Juice Scruggs at center and Christian Mahogany. He also said Blake Miller's knee is nothing serious. He explained why he kept the starters in late, using Miami as the cautionary example. Over the bye he wants the staff to work out who the team really is and who performs in critical moments, and he warned the performance won't be good enough for Green Bay.

The defense held Arizona to 1.8 yards per carry because everyone fit their gaps, and Campbell said making teams one-dimensional is the formula.
The group is trending up despite inconsistencies; Blake Miller and Tate Ratledge improve the more they play together.
The staff will spend the break working out the team's identity, its best players in critical moments, and the schematic tendencies defenses are catching on to, without overreacting to one result.
Campbell kept the starters in with a 21-point lead because he wanted the defense to finish together, citing a Miami game where pulling starters early backfired.
With Kennedy out, the team has no set replacement; they have in-house candidates and are looking outside the roster.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade & Texans vs. Jaguars
headline: Texans acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. (pending physical); David Montgomery is week-to-week with a groin injury, so Woody Marks should carry the RB load, and Jaylin Smith is also week-to-week.
summary: Ryans said Houston is excited to add Marvin Harrison Jr. as another playmaker. He pointed to the player's college production and his Ohio State rapport with C.J. Stroud as things that should help him settle in. Ryans credited Nick Caserio for the deal and said the approach is to add as many great players as possible. The trade is not official until Harrison passes his physical, which was expected that afternoon, and Ryans did not outline a role for him yet. He said he is not worried about Harrison learning the offense because of his work ethic. On injuries, David Montgomery (groin) is week-to-week, and Jaylin was put in the same category. Woody Marks stepped in with explosive runs and good vision, and Ryans said he will "continue to see more of that." Ryans praised Stroud's command, hot throws and protection of the ball, and called Will Anderson Jr. possibly the NFL's best defensive player right now. Rookie Kayden McDonald's debut was praised for stout interior play. The team's first win came on a better defensive showing, but Ryans said the penalties need to be cleaned up. Next up is Jacksonville, who just played in London, and Houston will travel Thursday evening.

injuries.detail: Groin injury; week-to-week, will miss time and Ryans will see how he progresses.
Ryans said "Jaylen" is in the same week-to-week category as Montgomery; the identification is uncertain (could be Jaylin Smith or Jaylin Noel).

signals.claim: Harrison will join the Texans after passing his physical and is expected to fit into the offense quickly.
signals.note: A new WR addition with a prior relationship with Stroud adds target competition in the Houston passing game, though his role is not yet defined.
signals.quote: He'll fit right in.

topics.detail: Ryans called the penalties unacceptable, noting that holding calls erased touchdowns and put the offense in worse field position. He said technique must improve.
Ryans said the first win came from execution in all three phases: physical run defense, third-down stops, a better special teams effort, and an offense that ran the ball and sustained drives.

The team leaves Thursday evening for London, arrives Friday and keeps its normal schedule. Ryans called Jacksonville a good team that plays fast and stops the run, and said Trevor Lawrence is playing well and Parker Washington is jumping off the tape.
Ryans said the front office tries to improve the team with whatever is available, and that adding receivers is not necessarily by design. The focus is on 2026.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 5 recap, Colts at Steelers
headline: Steichen praised Daniel Jones' ball security and poise, said teams are stacking the box on Jonathan Taylor so the scheme must open up the run and pass game, and is still building continuity with a reshuffled WR group ahead of Tennessee.
summary: Steichen called the loss disappointing, saying the offense moved the ball but failed to convert in the red zone, and the defense allowed two explosive plays (a 50-yarder and an 80-yarder) that led to touchdowns. He pushed back on questions about effort, saying Sauce Gardner and Akeem Davis-Gaither showed accountability and that tackling will get more emphasis in practice. On Jonathan Taylor, he acknowledged opponents are stacking the box and said the coaching staff must scheme him open in the run game and win one-on-ones and use play action in the pass game. He gave Daniel Jones a strong review: poised in the pocket, accurate throughout, and no turnovers, with the late drop in completion percentage blamed on chasing a two-score deficit. He said continuity with receivers takes time; Jones has a connection with Josh Downs and Tyler Warren, while Laquon Treadwell, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Keenan Allen are being worked in. The defense is last in the league in takeaways, and he stressed punching at the ball and drilling it daily. He also discussed the team's road struggles, culture, and the kicker's range affecting fourth-down decisions, and he closed by looking ahead to Tennessee.

signals.claim: Jones played a solid, accurate, turnover-free game and is the starting QB the offense is building around.
signals.note: Steichen's confidence and the clean ball security support Jones as a steady fantasy QB option, though late-game volume came from game script.

signals.claim: The staff will try to scheme Taylor open against stacked boxes and lean on play action and outside one-on-ones to offset it.
signals.note: Taylor is facing loaded boxes, so efficiency may be capped unless the passing game punishes defenses; Steichen gave no specific plan for new touches.

signals.claim: Downs has an established connection with Jones, which should keep him a primary target.
signals.note: His rapport with Jones suggests a stable target share even as other receivers are integrated.
signals.quote: Obviously he has a connection with Downs and Warren.

signals.claim: Warren has an established connection with Jones and should remain a key target.
signals.note: Rapport with the QB supports continued targets for the tight end.
signals.quote: Obviously he has a connection with Downs and Warren.

signals.claim: Treadwell is being worked into the passing game and practices are focused on building chemistry with him.
signals.note: Newer to the offense, so his role could grow as continuity builds, but it is not yet defined.
signals.quote: you got Treadwell in there now and we're working Treadwell in

signals.claim: Westbrook-Ikhine is among the receivers being integrated with Jones through practice reps.
signals.note: A crowded receiver group makes his target share uncertain.
signals.quote: we're working Treadwell in and Westbrook and Keenan.

signals.claim: Allen is among the receivers still building continuity with Jones.
signals.note: Part of a reshuffled receiver group, so his weekly usage remains uncertain.
signals.quote: we're working Treadwell in and Westbrook and Keenan.

topics.detail: Sauce Gardner and Akeem Davis-Gaither publicly questioned effort and desire; Steichen called it a positive that they showed accountability, but said tackling will get more drills and emphasis.
The defense is last in the league in turnovers forced. Steichen said he addressed it in the team meeting and wants a relentless approach to attacking the ball.
Pittsburgh used bubble screens and look routes early. Steichen said the defense must rally and tackle those, win one-on-ones on dropbacks, and coaches must scheme better matchups on pass-rush downs.
The offense moved the ball but did not convert in the red zone, while two explosive plays (50 and 80 yards) led to Pittsburgh touchdowns.
Steichen acknowledged the team's road record is poor and said small margins demand making plays. He defined culture as daily behaviors: character, preparation, consistency and relentlessness.
Steichen said the kicker's range factors into fourth-down decisions, with long fourth downs favoring a kick and short ones leading to going for it.

title: Andy Reid Speaks to the Media | Press Conference 10/12
headline: Tyquan Thornton is likely headed to IR; Xavier Worthy stays a key target, Cyrus Allen should see more work, and Kenneth Walker III continues to look good.
summary: Reid said there were no players in the building, so he had no real injury updates. He did say Tyquan Thornton will most likely go on IR, with Cam Jones elevated and Justin Watson signed to the practice squad. He expects Xavier Worthy to remain a target after a strong game, and he doesn't think Worthy's role changes much because he is already a big part of the pass game. He praised Thornton's work stretching the field, said Worthy can also do that, and said the other receivers will mix in because they all have speed. Cyrus Allen will probably work into the mix a bit more. Kingsley Suamataia, who sat out last week, is expected back, and the status of Josh and Richie will be clearer once they are back in tomorrow. Reid said the offense is scoring and has a good mix, and named short-yardage failures as the clear area to fix. He said Kenneth Walker III has not surprised him, since the team saw his full game in the playoffs. He described Justin Watson as fast, big, smart, and ready to contribute with a slight review. On defense, there have been no sacks in three games, but Reid said the pass rush is generating pressure.

Sat out last week; Reid said he'll be back in.

topics.detail: Reid likes the mix and the scoring, and named short-yardage failures as the main area to improve after the bye self-scout.
The team has no sacks in three games, but Reid pointed to consistent pressure as the important thing and believes the rush is generating it.
Cam Jones would be elevated if Thornton goes to IR, and Justin Watson was signed to the practice squad. Josh and Richie's practice status will be clearer once they are back in tomorrow.
Reid called the opposing defense good and said it has been in all its games despite its record, calling it a good challenge.

title: Jim Harbaugh on the Team's Determination to Improve and Win
headline: Ladd McConkey was only an emergency option vs. DEN but could work back into practice this week; Quentin Johnston stays limited, and Harbaugh owns two costly fourth-down calls.
summary: Harbaugh said his view of the loss hasn't changed. He regrets two fourth-down decisions, especially one, and apologized because he thinks he was wrong. Ladd McConkey was suited up but was only an emergency option at receiver, and Harbaugh is hopeful he can work back into practice this week. Quentin Johnston will likely be limited again, Brenen Thompson is working back into practice, and Tarheeb Still has a week-to-week hamstring injury but is starting to work back. He praised the offensive line, which had several rookies and three first-time starters, as very good for most of the game despite a few protection lapses late. On Justin Herbert's turnovers, he said Herbert is competing so hard that he forces plays in desperation, and he blamed himself for putting the QB in those spots. He explained his two second-quarter challenges (a short-yardage spot and a pass interference call) as worthwhile gambles on reviewable plays. He acknowledged the team needs to improve its complementary football, starting with turnovers, praised Akheem Mesidor and the outside linebackers, and stressed the team is determined to turn the season around.

signals.note: WR depth is thin, and his availability is uncertain until the end-of-week check.

topics.detail: Harbaugh said two fourth-down calls, especially one, did not give the team the best chance to win. He apologized and said he sincerely thinks he was wrong.

He challenged a short-yardage spot, hoping a view of the ball and knee would show forward progress, and a pass interference call that he and Del'Shawn Phillips believed involved a tipped ball. He said both were reviewable and worth the risk.
Harbaugh praised the young line, which included several rookies and three first-time starters, for protection and run blocking. He admitted a few protection issues late in the game.
He said the team must improve at complementary football, starting with turnovers, to stop giving the defense short fields. He said corrections are being made but declined to discuss them publicly.
Harbaugh said he is hell bent on turning the season around and that the Spanos family is in the fight with the team. He told players to keep being the leaders, believers and competitors.
Several injury answers were garbled in the captions. One player is undergoing testing and meeting with a specialist, and Harbaugh said they will see how the week goes.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 12, 2026
headline: Sirianni is 'hopeful' Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith return soon but gave no firm timeline; Dameon Pierce led a depleted RB room and drew praise, with Carson Steele, Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell as depth.
summary: Sirianni opened by taking responsibility for the end-of-game decisions in the loss to Jacksonville. He said he regrets how he handled the sequence after Jake Elliott's kick, specifically giving the ball back with eight seconds left, but defended the offense's two-minute work and the plan to move the ball forward to help the kicker. He said the offense as a whole has not been good enough and that players, coaches and he himself must improve. He also said injuries are no excuse and the focus is on finding solutions, though he acknowledged the offense is missing a lot of key players. On the 2-3 record, he said there is no panic in the building and compared the three-game skid to one the team had last year. On the injured skill players, he said he is hopeful Barkley and Smith get back but would not commit and said the week will tell. He said the running back room was a strength going into the season. With Barkley out and Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby lost during the game, he praised Dameon Pierce for his runs and pass protection and spoke well of Carson Steele, Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell. He defended Makai Lemon's out-of-bounds play on the final drive as not the reason for the loss.

topics.detail: Sirianni stands by the plan to advance the ball to ease the kicker's job and says the offense got the clock under 10 seconds. He regrets his own decision after the kick, giving the ball back with eight seconds left.
He said the offense has to be better across the board and that the staff is weighing what to cut or fix. He said injuries are not an excuse, and the focus is on solutions.
The team is 2-3, he sees no panic, and he is checking in with players daily.
Jalen Hurts is expected to execute the called play, and the coaches, not the quarterback, make the calls in end-of-game situations.

title: Kyle Shanahan: ‘We Have a Bunch of Warriors on This Team’
headline: 49ers beat Seattle in a grind-it-out win, but lost Dre Greenlaw early (no update) and Marques Sigle was also down. Mike Evans and Brock Purdy were the offensive engine, and Renardo Green had two picks.
summary: Shanahan called it a tough, emotional win in which the team showed grit in all three phases and never wavered after bad plays. Four defensive turnovers were the difference, and the defense limited explosive plays and defended the run well despite losing Dre Greenlaw early. Jaden Dugger stepped up in Greenlaw's absence, playing his base role and then a lot of nickel. Offensively, the 12-play, 75-yard touchdown drive stood out. Purdy and Mike Evans overcame penalties and bad down-and-distance with explosives, and Shanahan said that is exactly why Evans is here. Shanahan praised Purdy's fourth quarter and said Purdy kept finding Evans against coverages designed to take people away. He liked the offensive line's pass protection and run blocking. Renardo Green got two interceptions despite flu symptoms, and Malik Mustapha played the whole game in his return from a tough injury because Marques Sigle was down. On injuries, Jacob Cowing (ankle) and Khalid Kareem (stinger) returned to the game, Shanahan did not know the severity of a hamstring injury, and he said another player would not return this week.

injuries.detail: Had an ankle injury but returned to the game.
Had a stinger but returned to the game.
Left the game early and did not return. Shanahan did not describe the injury. When asked about a hamstring's severity he said "Don't know yet," and the transcript doesn't say whose hamstring it was.
Was "down" in the game, which opened up Mustapha's full-game workload. No details given.
Got sick with flu symptoms the night before but played and performed well.

signals.claim: Evans will remain a primary target in the Niners' passing game, with plays built to get him the ball when the right looks appear.
signals.note: Shanahan said many plays have Evans built in, Purdy hit him repeatedly, and Evans earned a game ball, which supports his fantasy value.
signals.quote: That's exactly why he's here.

signals.note: Shanahan praised Purdy's fourth quarter and his ability to find Evans against coverages that were taking people away.
signals.quote: a hell of a game by Brock.

signals.note: Dugger starts in base and played a lot of nickel after Greenlaw left, so he is a linebacker IDP to watch if Greenlaw misses time.
signals.quote: Dugger did an awesome job stepping it up.

signals.note: He left early and Shanahan gave no timeline. Monitor his status, since it affects Dugger and the linebacker corps.

signals.quote: he can be a very good corner in this league.

topics.detail: Shanahan called the team "a bunch of warriors" who love football and are not looking for stats or praise. He praised their composure after turnovers and penalties.
Four defensive turnovers decided the game. The punter was praised for a second straight strong week in the field position battle, and Shanahan said he could have gotten a game ball.
Shanahan said the line battled well against a tough defensive line. It gave Purdy time to throw a number of times and blocked well in the run game, though Seattle beat it on a few plays.
A player was ejected for allegedly headbutting an opponent without a helmet near the opposing bench. Shanahan did not object to the ejection and said the player has to be smarter.
Asked about a player's injury (name garbled in the transcript), Shanahan said he had no update but would probably have one tomorrow, and that he doesn't think the player returns this week.
Shanahan said the young defensive players, including Romello Height, stepped up a number of times, which was necessary given the Greenlaw loss and other defensive line absences.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/12/26
headline: Quinn was furious about the overtime clock-management collapse and gave no real fantasy news. Stefon Diggs and Nick Cross are 'encouraged' but their injury updates wait until Thursday, and Javontae Jean-Baptiste hurt his pick.
summary: Quinn opened by saying he was furious about the team's execution in crucial moments, especially the end of overtime. With about 56 seconds left and the team in field goal range after four missed kicks in the game, Washington handed off to Rachaad White to burn clock. Subbing, clock awareness and spiking the ball then took far too long. He took responsibility for the breakdown and said the play call from David Blough was not the problem, since the execution was. In hindsight he would not have subbed. He said the team meeting spent its time on the how and why, and that he does not think the locker room's confidence is eroded. On defense he praised how the game started and said Daron Payne was in the right spot on the zero-blitz drop, but he flagged touchdowns allowed late in the third and fourth quarters. He said the team had three false starts and will keep working cadence with an extra official in practice. On health, he was encouraged by medical reports on Stefon Diggs and Nick Cross, with a fuller update Thursday. He also said Javontae Jean-Baptiste hurt his pick (the injury is not yet clear, and the team is still gathering information). The next game is Monday night at San Francisco.

injuries.detail: Quinn is encouraged by medical reports and rehab progress, but will give a better update Thursday after seeing practice.
Quinn is encouraged by medical reports and rehab progress, with a fuller update Thursday depending on practice.

signals.note: Diggs's status is unresolved, so wait for Thursday's practice report before setting lineups.
signals.quote: I am encouraged based on, you know, guys, what I'm hearing from medical reports

signals.note: This was a clock-killing carry, not a usage change, so it says little about his role going forward.

topics.detail: Quinn blamed slow subbing, lack of urgency and failure to clock the ball after the 56-second handoff. He said that in hindsight they should not have subbed, and that the breakdown starts with him.
Quinn liked the start of the game but criticized touchdowns allowed late in the third and fourth quarters. He said Payne's zero-blitz drop is a designed technique to help against crossers.
Washington had three false starts. The team will keep working cadence and keep the extra official at practice to cut pre-snap penalties.

The R&D role was split in two: Kevin Brown handles replay and officiating, and Connor Nichol works on game management and analytics with David Blough. Quinn said he talks regularly with ownership and is not shut off from outside noise.
